You can still explore the portfolio below — it's here when you're ready.

rationale.title: Why this split?
rationale.subtitle: These weights come from a deterministic formula, not from the AI — every step is right here:
rationale.intro: Your risk score is <0>{{score}}/10</0>. The split is produced in two steps:
rationale.step1: <0>How much should stay on the safe side?</0><1/>As the risk score rises, the share of cash and bonds falls. For yours, the safe side came to <2>{{pct}}%</2> — this part cushions the shock in sharp downturns.
rationale.step2: <0>How was the remaining {{pct}}% shared out?</0><1/>Growth-side assets are weighted by their volatility (how much the price swings). At low risk scores the calm assets dominate; at high scores, the lively ones.
rationale.lowBand: Your score is on the low side, so the weight leans toward calm assets.
rationale.highBand: Your score is on the high side, so the weight leans toward lively assets.
rationale.midBand: You're in the middle, so the two are blended evenly.

rationale.footer: Your budget {{budget}} · split across at most {{cap}} assets · anything below {{minPct}}% was dropped (tiny positions are hard to track and contribute next to nothing)

reit.title: Real Estate Investing: REIT ETFs
reit.body: When your budget can't stretch to buying property outright, <0>REIT ETFs</0> let you invest in the real-estate market. They trade like stocks and hold dozens of commercial buildings and homes — you share in property returns without buying property.

XU100_IS.what: BIST 100 — an index of Türkiye's 100 largest listed companies, including giants like Turkish Airlines, Aselsan and BİM.
XU100_IS.why: As the Turkish economy grows, so does the value of these companies. The simplest way to invest in the local market.
XU100_IS.risk: Drops of 20-30% can happen in the short term. Over the long run (5+ years) the Turkish market has historically beaten inflation.

SPY.what: The S&P 500 — a basket of the 500 largest US companies. Apple, Google, Amazon and Tesla are all inside.
SPY.why: Dollar-based returns from one of the most consistently growing markets in history.
SPY.risk: It has been positive over the great majority of 10+ year windows — with exceptions: the 2000-2009 "lost decade" ended down. A long horizon usually suffices; it never guarantees.

QQQ.what: The Nasdaq 100 — a basket of the world's technology giants: Apple, Microsoft, NVIDIA, Meta and more.
QQQ.why: Tech has been the fastest-growing sector over the long run. Dollar-based, with high growth potential.
QQQ.risk: Tech stocks swing harder. Down 33% in 2022, up 55% in 2023 — it takes a strong stomach.

GLD.what: Physical gold in stock-market form. Instead of buying gold by the gram, you own a share of the dollar gold price.
GLD.why: Gold acts as a "safe haven" in crises. When stocks fall, gold often rises — it keeps your portfolio balanced.
GLD.risk: Gold doesn't grow as fast as stocks over the long run. But its power to preserve money is very high.

VNQ.what: Vanguard REIT ETF — a property basket investing in US commercial buildings, malls and housing.
VNQ.why: Even when a flat is out of budget, you can earn real-estate income with small amounts. Pays regular dividends, like rent.
VNQ.risk: Rising interest rates can weigh on property prices. And it isn't "touchable" the way physical property is.

SCHH.what: Schwab US REIT ETF — a housing-weighted American real-estate basket.
SCHH.why: Similar to VNQ but more housing-weighted. Property-market exposure with stock-like convenience.
SCHH.risk: REIT ETFs swing like stocks. But there's no buying-and-selling-property hassle, and you can cash out instantly.

stocks.what: An ownership share of a company or a basket of companies. As the business grows, so does your share.
stocks.why: The asset class with the highest long-run returns — growth potential well above inflation.
stocks.risk: Sharp short-term drops happen. Recovery has historically come most of the time, but it can take years.

gold.what: A precious metal that has held value for millennia. Known as "crisis insurance".
gold.why: When stocks fall, gold often rises. It helps your portfolio keep its balance.
gold.risk: It won't earn like stocks over the long run, but it stops your money from melting away.

fund.what: A pooled investment managed by professionals on your behalf, bought and sold through fund platforms.
fund.why: No need to pick individual stocks — experts manage the mix for you.
fund.risk: Management fees are deducted, and performance depends on the manager's decisions.

guide.title: First Investment Guide
guide.subtitle: Broker → Deposit → First order — a step-by-step guide for Türkiye

1.title: What Is a Broker?
1.body: To buy and sell stocks and funds you need a brokerage account. It's like a bank account, but for investing. In Türkiye every operating broker must hold an SPK (Capital Markets Board) licence.
1.tip: 💡 Verify the licence yourself on the regulator's official list (spk.gov.tr). We recommend no particular broker — we take commission from none of them.

2.title: How Do I Open an Account?
2.body:
1. Go to your chosen broker's website.
2. Tap "Open Account".
3. Enter your national ID number, email and phone.
4. Verify your identity by video call or at a branch.
5. The account activates within 1–3 business days.
2.tip: 💡 Most brokers support fully remote opening through their mobile app — no branch visit required.

3.title: How Do I Deposit Money?
3.body: Send money from your own bank account to the brokerage account by wire transfer. It usually shows up the same day or within 1 business day.
3.tip: 💡 Start small — 500–1,000 TL is plenty for a first try. You don't have to deposit everything at once.

4.title: How Do I Place the First Order?
4.body:
1. Go to the "Place Order" or "Buy" section in the app.
2. Search for the asset you want.
3. Enter the amount (lots / currency).
4. Choose "Market Order" — it fills at the current price.
5. Confirm.
4.tip: 💡 Important: if your portfolio includes ETFs listed on foreign exchanges (like SPY or QQQ), they don't trade on BIST. Your broker must offer overseas-market access, which usually needs a separate application and currency conversion. Before opening an account, ask: "can I buy foreign ETFs, and what's the commission?"

5.title: Tracking and Patience
5.body: After buying, don't build a habit of checking prices daily — it feeds anxiety. Once a week is enough. Lumos will let you know about big moves anyway.
5.tip: 💡 Golden rule: treat the money as if you won't see it for 5 years. Don't use funds you'll need short-term.

advisor.greeting:
Lumos Advisor.

Ask anything on your mind about investing or this app, in your own words — you're not limited to the canned questions. I explain concepts, walk you through the reasoning behind a portfolio decision, and put news in context.

One boundary: I won't say "buy" or "sell" for any specific stock or fund, and I won't predict where the market is going — nobody can honestly know those. Beyond that, nothing is off limits.

glossary.volatilite: How much the price swings up and down. High volatility = big waves; both risk and opportunity grow.
glossary.çeşitlendirme: Not putting all your eggs in one basket. Spread across different assets, one bad day can't take everything.
glossary.etf: A ready-made investment basket. One purchase makes you part-owner of dozens of stocks — no picking one by one.
glossary.fon: A pooled investment professionals manage on your behalf, bought and sold through fund platforms.
glossary.reit: A share of a real-estate company. A way to become a property investor with small amounts, without buying a flat.
glossary.temettü: Your share of a company's profit. Think of it like rent — it pays you for as long as you hold the stock.
glossary.risk skoru: Your 1-10 profile score. It shows how much turbulence you can stand; your portfolio is built around it.
glossary.likidite: How fast you can turn an asset into cash. Stocks take minutes; land can take months.
glossary.amortisman: An asset's loss of value over time. Inevitable for cars — which is why a car is an expense, not an investment.
glossary.enflasyon: Your money losing purchasing power. At 50% inflation, 100 under the mattress behaves like 67 a year later.
glossary.reel getiri: Your true gain after inflation. You made 45% but inflation was 60%? You actually lost.
glossary.drawdown: The biggest peak-to-trough fall. The answer to "how deep in the red were you on your worst day?"

etf.title: An ETF Is Really a Basket
etf.body: One purchase makes you part-owner of dozens of stocks. No picking them one by one — investing, pre-packaged.

diversification.title: Don't Put All Your Eggs in One Basket
diversification.body: Spread across different assets and one bad day can't take everything. That's called diversification.

inflation.title: Inflation Melts Your Money
inflation.body: At 50% inflation, 100 under the mattress behaves like 67 a year later. Not investing is a risk too.

dividend.title: A Dividend Is Like Rent
dividend.body: Your share of the company's profit. It pays you regularly for as long as you hold the stock — like renting out property.

reel-return.title: Real Return Is the True Gain
reel-return.body: You made 45% but inflation was 60%? You actually lost. Always look at the inflation-adjusted return.

liquidity.title: Liquidity Saves You
liquidity.body: Stocks turn to cash in minutes; land can take months. You might need money urgently — don't forget that.

drawdown.title: Drops Are Normal
drawdown.body: Markets often fall 10-15%. That's not panic, it's the natural cycle. No loss is locked in unless you sell.

gold.title: Gold Is Like Insurance
gold.body: In crises, gold usually rises while stocks fall. Think of it as your portfolio's "protective shield".

patience.title: Patience Is the Best Strategy
patience.body: The great majority of 10-year windows in S&P 500 history have been positive — though periods like 2000-2009 lost money. Time is your strongest tool, not a guarantee.

reit.title: Be a Landlord Without Buying a House
reit.body: REIT ETFs let you earn real-estate income with small amounts. A way to be a property investor without buying property.

fomo.title: FOMO Is Your Enemy
fomo.body: "Everyone's buying, so I will too" is the most dangerous sentence in investing. Buy every rally and you'll usually catch the top.

cost-avg.title: Regular Investing Lowers Risk
cost-avg.body: Investing the same amount monthly means buying cheap some months and dear in others. The result: a below-average cost.

goal.title: 🎯 My Goal
goal.subtitle: Let's turn a goal like "a house deposit in 3 years" into a concrete monthly plan.
goal.monthlyPlaceholder: How much do you save monthly right now? (opt.)
goal.alreadyOnTrack: Your existing savings reach the goal on their own — no extra contribution needed.
goal.needMonthly: To reach the goal on time you need to save about <0>{{amount}}</0> a month.
goal.realValueNote: Assuming {{inflation}}% inflation, your {{target}} goal will be worth ≈ <0>{{real}}</0> in today's money by then. A fixed target loses purchasing power over time — you may want to revisit it.
goal.onTrack: ✓ You're reaching the goal on time.
goal.delayed: At this pace your goal slips by about <0>{{months}} months</0>.
goal.howTitle: What is this calculation based on?
goal.howBody: It assumes the money you save doesn't sit idle but grows in a portfolio matching your risk profile, at an average {{growth}}% a year. That rate isn't invented: it's live inflation ({{inflation}}%) plus the real premium a diversified portfolio is assumed to earn over the long run. The horizon is converted to {{months}} months, and each contribution's growth over the remaining time is counted.
goal.howFormula: monthly = (target − grown value of current savings) × r / ((1+r)^months − 1),  r = monthly return
goal.howCaveat: This is a planning assumption, not a forecast: markets don't grow the same amount every year, and some years close down. If the rate turns out lower, the monthly figure won't be enough — reviewing the plan once a year is a good habit.
